title: Python Environment & Package Management
intro: Python environment and packaging questions come up at fresher interviews more than candidates expect — because companies have been burned by 'it works on my machine' and dependency conflicts. This page covers why virtual environments exist (each project gets its own isolated copy of Python dependencies so project A's Django 3.2 doesn't break project B's Django 4.2), how to create and activate a venv (python -m venv .venv, source .venv/bin/activate, the cross-platform difference between Mac/Linux and Windows activation), pip install and pip freeze for capturing installed packages, the requirements.txt workflow (pip freeze > requirements.txt, pip install -r requirements.txt — the standard handoff between developers), pyproject.toml as the modern evolution of requirements.txt and setup.py (concept-level — you don't need to write it from memory), and environment variables as the correct place to store secrets and configuration (never in code, never committed to Git).
